title: Continuous retraction onto minimal primes for a reduced ring with idempotent annihilators
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring which is reduced: $a^n=0$ for $n\geq1$ implies $a=0$. Assume that for every $a\in R$ there is $e_a\in R$ such that $e_a^2=e_a$ and $\{b\in R:ab=0\}=e_aR$. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $G\subseteq X$ be the set of minimal prime ideals, meaning primes containing no strictly smaller prime ideal. This is also the set of generic points [def-sc-generic-point] of the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$. Every prime $\mathfrak p$ contains exactly one minimal prime $r(\mathfrak p)$. With $G$ given the subspace Zariski topology, the map $r:X\to G$ is continuous and restricts to the identity on $G$. More precisely, for $D(a)=\{\mathfrak p\in X:a\notin\mathfrak p\}$ one has $r^{-1}(D(a)\cap G)=D(1-e_a)$ for every $a\in R$. The zero ring is allowed.

proof.text: The component description in Tag 00ES gives the irreducible components as $V(\mathfrak q)$ for minimal primes $\mathfrak q$. The point-closure formula gives $\overline{\{\mathfrak q\}}=V(\mathfrak q)$, so $\mathfrak q$ is their generic point by the definition of a generic point. Conversely a generic point $\mathfrak t$ of such a component satisfies $V(\mathfrak t)=V(\mathfrak q)$, hence $\mathfrak t=\mathfrak q$ by the inclusion criterion for point closures. Thus the two descriptions of $G$ in the statement agree.

proof.text: For any primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and idempotent $e$, one has $e\in\mathfrak q\Longleftrightarrow e\in\mathfrak p$. The forward implication is inclusion. If $e\in\mathfrak p$, then $1-e\notin\mathfrak p$, hence $1-e\notin\mathfrak q$; primality of $\mathfrak q$ applied to $e(1-e)=0$ gives $e\in\mathfrak q$. Also, in any prime $\mathfrak p$, exactly one of $e$ and $1-e$ belongs to $\mathfrak p$, by the same product-zero identity and their sum $1$.

Tag 00E0(4), applied to the zero ideal, supplies a minimal prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$. If $\mathfrak q,\mathfrak q'$ are both minimal under $\mathfrak p$, steps 2 and 3 give, for every $a\in R$, $a\in\mathfrak q\Longleftrightarrow e_a

otin\mathfrak q'\Longleftrightarrow a\in\mathfrak q'$. Thus $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q'$. Define $r(\mathfrak p)$ to be this unique minimal prime. For a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$, it itself is the unique one, so $r(\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak p$.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak q=r(\mathfrak p)$. Steps 2 and 3, followed by the last observation of step 3, give $a\notin\mathfrak q\Longleftrightarrow e_a\in\mathfrak q\Longleftrightarrow e_a\in\mathfrak p\Longleftrightarrow1-e_a\notin\mathfrak p$. This is precisely $r^{-1}(D(a)\cap G)=D(1-e_a)$.

source.place: Agent elementary membership calculation from steps 2-4; the retraction motivated by Hochster, after Proposition 5, pp.776-777.

proof.text: The basic-open basis theorem says every open $U\subseteq X$ is a union of sets $D(a)$, each open. By the definition of the subspace topology every open of $G$ is $U\cap G$, hence a union of the $D(a)\cap G$. Step 5 makes its inverse image the corresponding union of the open sets $D(1-e_a)$, proving continuity. Together with step 4 this is the required retraction. In the zero ring there is no proper prime ideal, since $0=1$; thus $X=G=\varnothing$, and the same assertion is the unique empty map, with all inverse images empty.
